strategy: Formalize the full selected mixed-precision block-Jacobi result, starting from a faithful construction of its finite-dimensional rounded operations and iterates, then deriving componentwise backward errors and the scalar recurrence with exactly the source constants. Use /spec/source.txt as authoritative and /spec/paper.tex as fallible proof guidance. A generic scalar recurrence theorem is a helper, never a substitute for constructing the matrix algorithm and deriving its hypotheses. For efficiency the final bound can absorb the correction norm using eta < 1 directly, avoiding an unnecessary matrix Neumann-series development; an optional resolvent construction H = (I-G)^(-1) must be justified if used. Prove the finite-k bound and limsup after establishing nonnegative alpha and beta. Previous feedback identifies an unresolved sorry, not a mathematical license to weaken the target. Preserve all linkage to A, D, N, b, x, computed Cholesky factors and the actual computed iterates; record precise source/model blockers rather than silently strengthening assumptions.

obligations.description: State the full result for arbitrary admissible dimensions, block sizes, matrices, exact solution, initial guess and rounded execution. Preserve A = D + N, SPD T-by-T diagonal blocks, S dividing n, u_s < u_c, defined gamma constants, no overflow/underflow, eta < 1, the exact definitions of c1,c2,G,eta,q,p,alpha,beta, the one-step bound, and both consequences under alpha < 1. Do not assume q < 1 or nonsingularity of A: neither is required.

Choose finite vector and matrix representations with explicit block indexing and flattening; realize the given block decomposition without changing n or T. Derive invertibility of D from its SPD blocks. Use the vector maximum norm and induced matrix infinity norm (maximum absolute row sum), with proved componentwise monotonicity and matrix-vector/product bounds. Do not accidentally use a matrix entrywise maximum norm or replace p by the larger product of two norms.

Construct or specify via operation-level execution semantics the two-precision algorithm: sequential products and accumulation within S-sized tiles, sequential reduction of tile sums, residual subtraction and solution addition at u_s, residual conversion to u_c, computed block Cholesky factorization and two triangular solves at u_c. Define xhat recursively from the initial iterate, and e(k) = xhat(k)-x. Per-operation relative error witnesses may instantiate the standard rounding model, but may not already assert the desired residual, solver, correction, or recurrence bounds.

Make explicit the mathematical content of precision, positive block sizes, valid gamma denominators, and completed computed factorization already implicit in the stated execution. The paper uses the S-tiled product although the selected statement does not expressly spell out its reduction order; its c1 requires that kernel. The earlier Cholesky helper explicitly assumes successful completion, while SPD alone does not guarantee floating-point Cholesky success. If these cannot be interpreted as part of the given computed execution, report the exact mismatch rather than add a new numerical condition or silently alter the theorem. Treat scalar delta symbols in the paper as component-dependent errors.

Prove the block dot-product backward error from elementary rounding and the product-of-error-factor gamma bound, including the two levels of sequential accumulation. With S dividing n, obtain zhat = (A + DeltaA)xhat and |DeltaA| <= gamma_(S+n/S-1;s)|A|. Keep S for dot-product tiling distinct from Cholesky block size T.

Construct the residual error witnesses from the actual subtraction: rhat = -A e + db + dz with |db| <= u_s|b| and |dz| <= c1|A||xhat|. Derive |rhat| <= |A||e| + u_s|b| + c1|A||xhat|. Construct the precision-conversion perturbation dr with |dr| <= u_c|rhat|, including the exact-conversion case.

Prove the earlier Cholesky-solve helper, or supply its full checked derivation from actual rounded factorization and forward/back substitutions. Assemble the block perturbations into DeltaD(k) and the actual computed block diagonal Rhat, showing (D+DeltaD(k)) chat(k+1) = rhat(k)+dr(k), and |DeltaD(k)| <= (gamma_(T;c)^2+3 gamma_(T+1;c)) |Rhat^T||Rhat|. Perturbations may depend on the right-hand side and iteration; no paper lemma may remain an axiom or an assumed algorithmic bound.

Define G from the actual D inverse and Rhat exactly as in the statement; prove entrywise nonnegativity and |D^(-1) DeltaD(k)| <= G. Derive bounds for D^(-1)db, D^(-1)dz, D^(-1)dr retaining the combined matrix |D^(-1)||A| that defines p. Establish eta,q,p,c1,c2 nonnegative and 1-eta positive before division.

Derive the correction identity from its perturbed system and D^(-1)A = I+D^(-1)N. If E=||e||, X=||xhat||, B=||D^(-1)|| ||b||, C=||chat|| and F=(1+u_c)(u_s B+c1 p X), derive (1-eta) C <= (1+q+u_c p) E+F, hence its division bound. This direct norm absorption establishes the required use of eta < 1 without needing H; if using H instead, construct its inverse, nonnegative entries and norm <= 1/(1-eta) rather than postulating them.

From the actual u_s addition obtain xhat_next=xhat+chat+dx+dc with |dx|<=u_s|xhat| and |dc|<=u_s|chat|. Combine the correction identity to retain the cancellation of e with the -e correction term. Bound E_next <= (q+u_c p)E + F + u_s X +(eta+u_s) C. Substitute the correction bound and check rational coefficient identities with 1-eta > 0 to obtain the paper intermediate bound, then use X <= ||x||+E to recover exactly the specified alpha and beta.

Prove alpha,beta >= 0, then use induction on k for the geometric-sum bound from the derived one-step inequality. Under alpha < 1, evaluate the sum including k=0, prove alpha^k tends to zero using 0 <= alpha < 1, establish boundedness of the real error-norm sequence and justify its limsup bound beta/(1-alpha). Include these in the full selected theorem, not merely as a separate unattached scalar result.
